renders._yaml:
- component: card
  id: ts_tv
  title: Transition to transversion ratio
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median transition to transversion (Ts/Tv) ratio over the callsets in view, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers whether the substitutions of a callset look like real variation.
    How to read: callsets of one data type should sit close together, so a callset far from the others points to false calls or a different sample or region. No cut-off is drawn, because the expected ratio depends on the data type (exome, genome or RNA) and no single source gives one for every callset. Open the table to compare callsets, then the FILTER breakdown for the calls that were removed.
  column: ts_tv
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread across callsets
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: pass_calls
  title: PASS calls per callset
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of calls that passed every filter, over the callsets in view. It answers how large a typical callset is once the caller's own filters are applied.
    How to read: a callset with far fewer calls than the others points to low coverage, a failed run or an over-strict filter. Compare it with the share of calls kept before deciding which.
    Source: https://samtools.github.io/hts-specs/VCFv4.3.pdf
  column: pass_calls
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread across callsets

- component: card
  id: pass_share
  title: Share of calls kept
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percentage of calls a caller kept, over the callsets in view. A call is kept when its FILTER field is PASS, meaning it passed every filter.
    How to read: a low share means the caller's hard filters removed many calls, which is common in noisy data such as RNA. A share that differs a lot between callsets of one cohort suggests a quality difference, so open the FILTER breakdown to see which filters removed the calls.
    Source: https://samtools.github.io/hts-specs/VCFv4.3.pdf
  column: pass_pct
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread across callsets

- component: card
  id: het_hom
  title: Heterozygous to homozygous ratio
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median ratio of heterozygous to homozygous-alternate genotype calls, over the callsets in view. It answers whether the genotype mix is similar from callset to callset.
    How to read: a callset whose ratio departs from the others can point to contamination, a sample swap, or a caller or filter difference. No cut-off is drawn, because the expected ratio depends on the population and the data type. Open the table to find the callset.
  column: het_hom_ratio
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread across callsets

- component: advanced_viz
  id: tstv_vs_hethom
  title: Substitution ratio against genotype ratio
  description: |-
    Each point is a callset: its heterozygous to homozygous-alternate ratio on the horizontal axis and its transition to transversion ratio on the vertical axis, coloured by caller. It answers whether a callset is an outlier on either measure.
    How to read: callsets of one data type should form a tight group. A point apart from the group on one axis points to a genotype issue, on the other axis to noisy substitutions, and a callset of one caller that sits apart from the other callers points to a caller effect. With few callsets, read the table instead, since neither ratio has a cut-off that holds for every data type.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median transition to transversion ratio of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of the caller.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Heterozygous to homozygous-alternate ratio
    y_title: Transition to transversion ratio
    top_n_labels: 10
    legend_pos: bottom
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
  roles:
    x: het_hom_ratio
    y: ts_tv
    label: sample
    color: caller

- component: table
  title: Callset table
  description: |-
    Each row is a callset (a sample and the caller that produced it) with its counts of calls, PASS calls, SNVs, indels and multiallelic sites, its Ts/Tv ratio, its genotype counts and its median quality, depth and heterozygous allele fraction. It answers which callset to inspect further.
    How to read: sort by the share of calls kept, by Ts/Tv or by the genotype ratio to find outliers, and compare callsets of the same caller.

- component: figure
  id: filter_bars
  title: FILTER values per callset
  description: |-
    Each bar is a callset, split into segments by FILTER value and sized by the share of its calls. It answers which filters removed the calls the caller did not keep.
    How to read: a large PASS segment means most calls were kept. A large segment of one hard filter points to what limits the callset, for example low quality or clustered SNPs, and the same filter dominating every callset points to the data or the caller settings rather than to one sample.
    Source: https://samtools.github.io/hts-specs/VCFv4.3.pdf
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: calls_pct
    color: filter_label
    labels:
      sample: Sample
      calls_pct: Share of calls (%)
      filter_label: FILTER value

- component: card
  id: calls_by_filter
  title: Calls by FILTER value
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total count of calls over the callsets in view, and the bars rank the FILTER values that hold the most of them. It answers which filters account for most of the calls.
    How to read: PASS at the top is the usual picture. When a hard filter outranks PASS, the caller's filters are removing more than they keep, so check the filter definitions in the VCF header.
    Source: https://samtools.github.io/hts-specs/VCFv4.3.pdf
  column: calls
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: filter_label
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: the largest FILTER values, with the median and largest per callset

- component: table
  title: FILTER table
  description: |-
    Each row is a callset and a FILTER value, with the number of calls, their share of the callset and how many are SNVs and indels. It answers how many calls each filter removed in each callset.
    How to read: sort by share of calls to see the dominant filters, and filter on a FILTER value to compare it across callsets.

- component: figure
  id: spectrum_bars
  title: Substitution spectrum per callset
  description: |-
    Each bar is the share of a callset's PASS SNVs in one of the six pyrimidine substitution classes. It answers whether the pattern of base changes looks like genetic variation or carries a signature of its own.
    How to read: the classes are folded so that, for example, a G to A change counts with C to T. In an RNA callset, an excess of T to C comes from adenosine-to-inosine editing, which is read as A to G, and a DNA callset of the same individual would not show it. Compare callsets of the same data type, and open the Ts/Tv card for the transition share.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25859542/
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: substitution_class
    y: fraction
    color: sample
    barmode: group
    labels:
      substitution_class: Substitution
      fraction: Share of PASS SNVs
      sample: Sample

- component: card
  id: transition_share
  title: Transitions and transversions
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total count of PASS SNVs over the callsets in view, and the bar splits them into transitions and transversions. It answers how the base changes divide between the two kinds.
    How to read: a callset with a very different split from the others points to a sample, caller or data type difference. Open the spectrum for the class behind it.
  column: count
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: mutation_class
  caption: split by mutation class, with the median and largest class count

- component: table
  title: Substitution table
  description: |-
    Each row is a callset and a substitution class, with its SNV count, its share of the callset and whether the class is a transition or a transversion. It answers how many SNVs fall in each class.
    How to read: filter on a class to compare it across callsets, or sort by share to find the dominant class.

- component: card
  id: density_windows
  title: Variants per window
  description: |-
    The hero number is the largest count of distinct PASS variants in a single window, and the box shows the quartiles over all windows. It answers how dense variation is and how uneven it is along the genome.
    How to read: a maximum far above the box marks a hot spot, such as a region of high diversity or of mapping artefacts. Open the karyotype or the track to see where it sits.
  column: value
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: the densest window, with the spread over all windows

- component: advanced_viz
  id: density_karyotype
  title: Variant density along chromosomes
  description: |-
    Each band is a window on a chromosome, shaded on a continuous scale by the count of distinct PASS variants it holds. It answers where along the genome the variants of each sample concentrate.
    How to read: dark bands are dense and pale bands are sparse, so a dark band shared by every sample suggests a region that differs from the reference assembly. A band dense in one sample only points to that sample. Open the track to read the counts.
  kind: ideogram
  roles:
    chrom: chrom
    start: start
    end: end
    value: value
    sample: sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: density_track
  title: Variant density track
  description: |-
    Each bar is a window along a chromosome, with the count of distinct PASS variants in it as its height, one trace per sample. It answers how density changes along a chromosome and whether samples agree.
    How to read: traces that rise and fall together point to regions of the genome that vary in every sample. A trace that departs from the others over a stretch points to a sample-specific event or to a coverage difference.
  kind: coverage_track
  roles:
    chromosome: chrom
    position: start
    end: end
    value: value
    sample: sample

- component: table
  title: Density table
  description: |-
    Each row is a window on a chromosome with its start, its end, the count of distinct PASS variants and the sample. It answers which windows hold the most variants.
    How to read: sort by count to find the densest windows, and filter by chromosome or sample.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: vaf_against_depth
  title: Allele fraction against read depth
  description: |-
    Each point is a variant call: its read depth on the horizontal axis and its variant allele fraction on the vertical axis, coloured by caller. It answers whether the calls rest on enough reads and whether their allele balance is plausible.
    How to read: a heterozygous germline variant sits near an allele fraction of 0.5 and a homozygous-alternate one near 1.0, so calls scattered between the two bands, especially at low depth, are less reliable. Allele balance in RNA is often skewed by expression, so read the bands loosely there. Compare callers to see whether one produces more calls off the bands, and note that no cut-off is drawn, since no source gives one for every data type.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    x_title: Read depth
    y_title: Variant allele fraction
    top_n_labels: 5
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    x: dp
    y: vaf
    label: variant_key
    color: caller

- component: advanced_viz
  id: variant_rainfall
  title: Allele fraction along the genome
  description: |-
    Each point is a variant call at its position along the chromosomes, with its variant allele fraction as the height, coloured by caller. It answers where along the genome the calls cluster and whether their allele balance changes by region.
    How to read: horizontal lines of points at the same height are the usual genotype bands. A stretch where calls are dense and off the bands can mark a copy number change, a mapping problem or a hot spot of artefacts. Switch the colour to the sample to see whether it is shared.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the 95th percentile of the allele fraction in this table, a reference defined by the data and not a cut-off from any source.
  kind: manhattan
  config:
    score_kind: Variant allele fraction
    highlight: none
    score_threshold_stat: p95
    color_by_columns:
    - caller
    - sample
    default_color_by: caller
    hover_cols:
    - dp
    - qual
    top_n_labels: 5
  roles:
    chr: chrom
    pos: pos
    score: vaf
    feature: variant_key

- component: advanced_viz
  id: variant_genome_view
  title: Variant calls along the genome
  description: |-
    Each point is a variant call at its position, with its allele fraction as the height, coloured by variant type, with one lane per caller. It answers where each caller makes calls and whether callers agree on a region.
    How to read: a region with calls in one lane and none in the others is a locus the callers disagree on. Colours separate SNPs from insertions and deletions, so a run of indels in one lane may be a homopolymer error. Zoom to a locus and open the table for the calls.
  kind: genome_view
  config:
    score_title: Variant allele fraction
    top_stars: 0
  roles:
    chr: chrom
    pos: pos
    score: vaf
    feature: variant_key
    sample: caller
    category: variant_type

- component: card
  title: Call quality
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median QUAL value of the calls in view, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how much confidence the caller put in its calls.
    How to read: a low median or a box reaching down to small values means many weak calls. The scale of QUAL depends on the caller, so compare callers only against their own runs, and filter on PASS to see the kept calls.
  column: qual
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread across calls

- component: card
  title: Read depth at calls
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median read depth at the calls in view, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers how well covered the called sites are.
    How to read: a box reaching down to a depth of a few reads means many calls rest on little evidence, and a very long upper whisker marks repeats or collapsed regions. Open the depth against allele fraction plot to see how that affects the allele balance.
  column: dp
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread across calls

- component: card
  title: Variant allele fraction
  description: |-
    The hero number is the mean variant allele fraction of the calls in view, and the box shows their quartiles. It answers where the allele balance sits overall.
    How to read: a mix of heterozygous and homozygous-alternate calls pulls the mean between 0.5 and 1.0, so it moves with the genotype mix more than with quality. Use the histogram below to see the two bands.
  column: vaf
  aggregation: average
  aggregations:
  - median
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: average and median, with the spread across calls

- component: figure
  title: Allele fraction distribution
  description: |-
    Each bar counts the variant calls in a bin of allele fraction, split by caller. It answers whether the allele balance shows the expected genotype bands.
    How to read: peaks near 0.5 and near 1.0 are the heterozygous and homozygous-alternate genotypes of a diploid sample. A mass of calls at low fractions suggests noise, mosaicism or contamination, and callers whose histograms differ are making different calls on the same data.
  visu_type: histogram
  dict_kwargs:
    x: vaf
    color: caller
    labels:
      vaf: Variant allele fraction
      caller: Caller

- component: table
  title: Variant table
  description: |-
    Each row is a variant call with its locus, alleles, quality, FILTER status, genotype, read depth and allele fraction. It answers which calls to inspect or follow up.
    How to read: filter on FILTER status or sort by depth or quality to find weak calls, and use the variant key to look a call up in a genome browser.
